activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A well-run session gets real insight instead of polite or leading answers.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in discovery and acceptance testing and feeds research reports and analysis. It is often observed by teammates for shared learning.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Prepare a light guide, then ask open questions and listen more than you talk. Run remote sessions over Zoom and take careful notes.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Secondary research is learning from what others have already published, rather than gathering new data yourself. It is standing on existing knowledge.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: It is a fast, cheap way to get grounded before investing in new studies.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs through discovery and acceptance testing and feeds journey maps, research reports, and analysis. It often kicks off a research effort.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Gather trustworthy sources and pull out what is relevant to your questions. Organize the findings in FigJam or a spreadsheet.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Card sorting asks people to group and label items the way that makes sense to them. It reveals how users naturally organize information.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: It helps a team structure a product to match how users think, not how the team happens to.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It feeds research plans and analysis and shapes information architecture like sitemaps. It can run as a group activity or a remote study.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Give participants items to sort into groups they name. Run it in Optimal Workshop or UXtweak, then look for common patterns.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Interviewing is talking one-on-one with users to understand their needs, goals, and frustrations. It is the most direct way to learn from people.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Nothing beats hearing directly from users for understanding what they actually need.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in discovery and feeds the research report. Teammates often observe to build shared understanding.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Prepare open questions, then listen closely and follow curiosity. Run remote interviews on Zoom and record with permission.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Surveys collect answers from many people through a set of questions. They trade depth for reach.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Surveys show how common a need or opinion is across a larger group.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: They run in discovery and acceptance testing and feed research reports, plans, and analysis. They pair well with interviews for depth plus breadth.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Write clear, unbiased questions and keep it short. Use a survey tool, then analyze the results in a spreadsheet.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Storyboarding tells the story of a user's experience as a series of simple frames, like a comic strip. It shows the experience in real-life context.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: It helps a team imagine the situation around a product, not just the screens, sparking more human ideas.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in discovery and produces the storyboard, building on personas and journey maps. It is often sketched together.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Draw the key moments of a user's story, frame by frame. Use Figma or FigJam and keep the sketches rough and quick.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Product positioning is deciding how a product presents itself and stands out from alternatives. It shapes the story customers hear.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A clear position helps everyone tell a consistent story and helps customers see why the product is for them.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs across discovery, vision, and launch and feeds positioning statements, the value proposition, and marketing. It is often shaped with the team.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Define who the product is for and why it is different, in a sentence or two. Refine it in Notion with the team until it is sharp.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

activities.Activity Description: A diary study asks people to log their experiences over days or weeks. It captures real life as it unfolds, not just a snapshot.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: It reveals patterns and moments that a single session would miss.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in discovery and feeds the research report. It complements interviews with over-time insight.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Ask participants to record entries at set moments, then review for patterns. Collect entries in FigJam or a spreadsheet.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: A contextual inquiry is observing and talking with users in their real environment while they work. It studies people where things actually happen.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Seeing real context reveals needs and workarounds people would never think to mention.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in discovery and feeds the research report. Teammates often observe to learn firsthand.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Watch users in their setting and ask about what they do as they do it. Take notes in Notion or FigJam, or record over Zoom.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Ethnographic observation is watching how people behave in their natural setting, with minimal interference. You learn by seeing, not just asking.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: People often do things differently from how they describe them, and observation catches that gap.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs in discovery and acceptance testing and feeds research reports, plans, and analysis.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Spend time watching real behavior and note what surprises you. Capture observations in Notion or a spreadsheet.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Usability testing watches real people try to use a design to see where they succeed and struggle. It puts the design to the test with actual users.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: It gives hard evidence about what works, so fixes target real problems, not guesses.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs in discovery and acceptance testing and feeds usability test reports, research reports, and analysis. It often loops right back into design.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Give people real tasks and watch without helping, then note where they get stuck. Run sessions on Zoom or Maze and summarize the findings.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Prototype concept testing puts an early prototype in front of users to check whether an idea works before building it. It tests the concept, not the polish.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Testing early saves the team from building something users do not actually want.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It feeds research reports, plans, and analysis and loops back into design. It is a core agile habit of learning before committing.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Show the prototype, give a task, and watch the reaction. Use Maze or Zoom, then feed what you learn back into the design.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: A/B prototype test creation builds two versions of a design so you can compare which works better. It sets up a head-to-head test.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Comparing real options with users settles debates with evidence instead of opinion.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in the Implement work and produces the prototypes being tested. It supports usability and concept testing.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Make two clear variations that differ in one meaningful way. Build them in Figma and set them up for testing in Maze or Dovetail.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: UI kit creation is building the shared set of interface styles and elements a product uses. It is the toolbox designers pull from.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A shared kit keeps a product consistent and speeds up design work.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in the Implement work and produces the design system and component library.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Define the core styles and elements, then build them cleanly as reusable pieces in Figma so the team can share them.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Developing information architecture is organizing a product's content and structure so people can find things. It is the blueprint for how a product is arranged.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Good structure is the difference between a product that feels obvious and one where people get lost.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in the Implement work and produces prototypes, sitemaps, and taxonomy.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Map the content into logical groups and a clear hierarchy. Sketch the structure in Figma or FigJam and test it with users.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Prototype creation is building an interactive version of a design that people can click through. It makes an idea feel real before it is built.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A prototype lets the team test a real experience early and cheaply.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in the Implement work and produces wireframes and prototypes at different levels of polish.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Turn your designs into clickable screens in Figma. Keep it just real enough to test the questions you care about.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Tracking milestone progress is keeping an eye on how the project is moving against its goals. It is the regular pulse-check on the work.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: It helps a team spot slippage early and adjust before small delays become big ones.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens across the project and feeds the Gantt chart and roadmap. It supports steady, visible agile delivery.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Check what is done against the plan and note what is at risk. Update the roadmap in Notion so everyone can see where things stand.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

activities.Activity Description: Tracking epic progress is following how a large body of work is advancing toward completion. It keeps big efforts from stalling unseen.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: It gives the team and stakeholders a clear view of progress on the things that matter most.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in the Vision work and feeds the roadmap. It supports product ownership.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Break the epic into visible pieces and mark progress as they finish. Track it in Notion or Trello.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

activities.Activity Description: A UX heuristics analysis reviews a design against well-known usability rules to catch obvious problems. It is an expert gut-check for the experience.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: It quickly surfaces common issues without needing a full study.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in requirements and implement and feeds the UX audit report.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Walk through the product against a checklist of usability principles, noting each violation. Record findings in FigJam or a spreadsheet.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Product roadmap maintenance is keeping the roadmap current as plans and priorities change. A roadmap only helps if it stays honest.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: An up-to-date roadmap keeps everyone aligned and expectations realistic.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in the Vision work and keeps the roadmap accurate. It is revisited often as the team learns.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Review the roadmap regularly, adjust for what changed, and communicate updates. Keep it in Notion or Trello.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

activities.Activity Description: Market research is learning about the market, customers, and competitors a product operates in. It reads the landscape a product enters.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: It grounds big decisions in evidence about real demand rather than hunches.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs across discovery, vision, and launch and feeds the business plan, positioning, and go-to-market work.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Gather data on customers and competitors and pull out the patterns. Organize findings in Notion for the team.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

activities.Activity Description: Scheduling meetings is lining up the right people at the right time to move work forward. It sounds simple but keeps a team in sync.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Well-run, well-timed meetings keep everyone aligned without wasting people's time.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens across the project and produces meeting agendas. It supports project management.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Find a time that works, set a clear agenda, and invite only who is needed. Use Notion and Zoom to organize and host.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

activities.Activity Description: QA testing is checking that a product works as intended before it reaches users. It is the safety net that catches bugs.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Shipping something broken costs far more than catching it early, in money and trust.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in launch and acceptance testing and produces the QA test plan, cases, and analysis. In agile work it happens continuously, not just at the end.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Run through the test cases and log anything that fails. Track issues in Notion or a spreadsheet and confirm fixes.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

activities.Activity Description: Autotest creation is writing tests that a computer runs automatically to check a product. It lets the same checks run over and over without manual effort.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Automated tests catch problems fast every time code changes, which keeps quality steady.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in launch and produces QA test cases. It supports ongoing quality as the product grows.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Identify the checks worth automating, then write tests that run them. Manage them in Notion and your code tools.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

activities.Activity Description: Tracking sprint progress is watching how a sprint is going day to day. It keeps the current cycle honest.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A daily read on progress lets the team adjust before the sprint runs out.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs across sprints and feeds the burn down chart, refined backlog, and sprint plan.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Check what is done and what is stuck each day. Update the board in Notion or Trello and raise blockers early.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

activities.Activity Description: User acceptance testing checks whether the finished work actually meets users' and stakeholders' needs. It is the final does-this-really-work check.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: It confirms the product does what people need before it goes live, protecting against costly misses.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs across discovery, implement, launch, and acceptance testing and feeds research reports and stakeholder feedback.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Have real users try the work against the agreed criteria and note gaps. Capture results in Notion or Trello.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Roles: Product Ownership, UX (User Experience) Design, UX (User Experience) Research, UX (User Experience) Writing
activities.Activity Description: Facilitating agile workshops is guiding a group session so the team collaborates well and reaches a clear outcome. The facilitator holds the space, not the answers.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Well-run workshops turn a room of individuals into shared thinking and real decisions.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in discovery and implement and supports many deliverables. Workshops are where a lot of agile collaboration happens.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Plan a clear goal and a few activities, then guide the group and keep everyone involved. Run it in FigJam or over Zoom.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

activities.Activity Description: Clickable prototype creation is making a design you can actually click through, so it behaves like a real product. It brings a static design to life.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A clickable version lets people experience a flow and gives far better feedback than a picture.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in the Implement work and produces prototypes at different levels of polish.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Link your screens so taps lead somewhere in Figma. Add just enough interaction to test the flow.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Coaching teammates is helping others grow by guiding rather than directing. A coach helps people find their own way forward.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Growing people strengthens the whole team and builds independence over time.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens at intake and produces the personal growth roadmap. It supports agile coaching throughout a project.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Ask questions that help someone reflect, and support their next step. Use Notion to track goals and Zoom to meet.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

activities.Activity Description: Threat modeling is thinking through how a system could be attacked so you can defend it. It is imagining trouble on purpose.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Finding weaknesses before attackers do protects users and their data.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It feeds the network architecture and supports information security work.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Map the system, list how it could be attacked, and rank the risks. Capture the model in Notion.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: OWASP, the open community for software security: https://owasp.org/

activities.Activity Description: Penetration testing is safely trying to break into a system to find its weak spots. It is a controlled attack to expose gaps.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Real-world testing reveals holes that reviews on paper miss.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It feeds the network architecture and supports security work.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: With permission, probe the system for vulnerabilities and document each one. Record findings in Notion.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: OWASP, the open community for software security: https://owasp.org/

activities.Activity Description: Firewall configuration is setting the rules for what traffic a system allows or blocks. It is the gatekeeper for a network.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A well-configured firewall keeps out unwanted access while letting the right traffic through.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It feeds the network architecture and supports security work.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Define which traffic is allowed and block the rest, then test the rules. Document the setup in Notion.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: OWASP, the open community for software security: https://owasp.org/

activities.Activity Description: Security protocol definition is setting the rules and procedures that keep a system safe. It is the security playbook.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Clear protocols mean the team handles data and access safely and consistently.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It feeds the network architecture and supports security work.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Define the rules for access, data handling, and response, and write them clearly. Keep them in Notion for the team.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: OWASP, the open community for software security: https://owasp.org/

activities.Activity Description: An information security audit reviews a system to check how well it is protected. It is a health check for security.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Regular audits catch weaknesses before they become breaches.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It feeds the network architecture and supports security work.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Review the system against security standards and note gaps. Record findings in Notion or a spreadsheet.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: OWASP, the open community for software security: https://owasp.org/

activities.Activity Description: Sprint retrospective facilitation is guiding the team's reflection at a sprint's end on what went well and what to improve. It is how a team learns from itself.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Retrospectives are where continuous improvement actually happens, so the team gets better each cycle.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens across sprints and produces retro action items and maturity measurements. It is a team workshop.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Create a safe space, gather honest reflections, and agree on a few changes. Run it in FigJam or Trello.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

activities.Activity Description: Sprint demo facilitation is running the session where the team shows the work they finished. It makes progress visible and invites feedback.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Demos keep stakeholders aligned and build trust by showing real progress.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens across sprints and produces the sprint demo presentation.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Prepare a short walk-through of the completed work and invite feedback. Present it in Notion or with presentation tools.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

activities.Activity Description: Identifying research patterns is spotting the themes that repeat across research. It is finding the signal in the noise.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Patterns tell the team what is common and important, so they act on real trends.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in discovery and acceptance testing and feeds research analysis.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Review your findings and group what repeats into clear themes. Cluster them in FigJam.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Experiment design is planning a study so its results are fair and trustworthy. It sets up research to actually answer the question.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A well-designed experiment gives answers you can trust instead of misleading results.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in discovery and produces the research plan.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Define your question, what you will measure, and who you will study. Plan it in Notion or UXtweak.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Technical architecture creation is designing how a system will be built and fit together. It is the structural blueprint for the product.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A sound architecture lets a product scale and stay stable, while a shaky one causes trouble later.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in requirements and feeds the system architecture, diagrams, specs, and database design.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Map the major parts and how they connect, weighing trade-offs. Draw it in FigJam and document it in Notion.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

activities.Activity Description: Inventorying content is making a full list of the content a product has or needs. It is a stocktake of everything written.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Knowing what content exists reveals gaps and duplicates, so nothing important is missing.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in the Implement work and produces the content inventory and outline.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: List every piece of content and note its status. Track it in a spreadsheet or Notion.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Developing a go-to-market strategy is planning how a product will launch and reach its audience. It ties product, marketing, and sales into one plan.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A strong launch plan gives good work its best shot at landing with real users.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs across discovery, vision, and launch and feeds marketing, positioning, and the go-to-market plan.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Define the audience, message, channels, and timing for launch. Build the plan in Notion or FigJam with the team.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

activities.Activity Description: Customer segmentation is splitting a broad audience into smaller groups that share needs or traits. It reveals the distinct kinds of people you serve.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Knowing the segments lets a team tailor a product and message instead of pleasing no one by aiming at everyone.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs across discovery, vision, and launch and feeds personas, positioning, and marketing.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Group your audience by shared needs or behavior and name each segment. Map them in Notion or FigJam.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

activities.Activity Description: Price testing is checking what customers are willing to pay for a product. It finds the price that works for buyers and the business.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: The right price can make or break whether a product succeeds financially.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in discovery and feeds the business plan and go-to-market plan.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Try different price points with real or potential customers and watch the response. Track results in Notion.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

activities.Activity Description: Documenting code is explaining how a product's code works so others can understand it. It is the manual for the software.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Good documentation lets new developers get up to speed and keeps knowledge from vanishing.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It produces code and coding documentation and supports the whole codebase.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Write clear notes on what the code does and how to use it, right alongside it. Manage it in GitHub.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

activities.Activity Description: Deploying code is releasing software so it runs live for users. It is the step that gets the work into the world.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Smooth, reliable deployment is how finished work actually reaches people.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It produces code and supports launch. In agile work, teams deploy often in small pieces.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Package the code and release it through your pipeline, then confirm it runs. Manage releases in GitHub.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

activities.Roles: Scrum Master, Product Ownership, Product Operations
activities.Activity Description: Defining team process is deciding how a team will get work done, step by step. It makes the way of working clear.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A clear process reduces confusion and friction, so work flows smoothly.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens at intake and produces Kanban board statuses and the team process map.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Map how work should move from idea to done and agree on it. Set it up in Notion or FigJam.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Team Playbook, practical plays for healthy teamwork: https://www.atlassian.com/team-playbook

activities.Activity Description: Customer experience mapping traces a customer's whole relationship with a product across every touchpoint. It zooms out to the full picture.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Seeing the experience as a whole keeps improvements in one place from causing problems in another.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in discovery and implement and produces journey maps and customer experience diagrams.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Chart each touchpoint and how it feels for the customer. Build the map in Figma or FigJam.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Creating presentations is turning ideas or results into clear slides for sharing. It helps a team walk others through their thinking.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A clear presentation gets an idea understood and remembered.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens across the project and produces the sprint demo presentation. It is a shared skill across roles.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Outline the key points, then build simple, focused slides. Use presentation tools and keep the story clear.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

activities.Activity Description: Entity relationship creation is mapping the data a product stores and how the pieces connect. It is a blueprint for a database.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Getting the data structure right early prevents tangled databases that are painful to fix.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It produces the database architecture and supports development.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Identify the data items and how they relate, then diagram them. Draw it in FigJam and document in Notion.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

activities.Activity Description: Creating AI prompts is writing clear instructions that get useful results from an AI tool. It is a practical skill everyone can use.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A good prompt is the difference between AI that helps and one that wastes time.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens across the project and produces the AI prompt. It supports many activities rather than one role.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: State clearly what you want, give context, and refine based on what you get back. Use your AI model of choice and iterate.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

activities.Activity Description: Creating REST APIs is building the connections that let different pieces of software talk to each other. It is how systems share data and features.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Well-built APIs let parts of a product and outside services work together reliably.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It produces code and supports development.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Design clear endpoints, build them, and test each one. Develop and manage them in your IDE and GitHub.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

activities.Activity Description: SEO design is shaping a product or site so it shows up when people search for it. It is about being findable, not just good.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Even great content helps no one if people cannot find it.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in the Implement work and produces the SEO strategy.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Research the terms people search, then structure content and pages around them. Plan it in Notion or FigJam.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Creating research plans is laying out what you want to learn, how, and from whom. It is the blueprint for a study.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Planning first keeps research focused and trustworthy, so you get clear answers.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in discovery and produces task analyses, affinity maps, and the research plan.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Define your questions, methods, and participants clearly. Write the plan in Notion or FigJam.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Rapid ideation is quickly generating lots of ideas without judging them yet. It is about quantity first, quality later.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Getting many ideas out fast helps a team escape the obvious first answer.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in the Implement work and produces sketches and strategy definitions. It is often a group workshop.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Set a short timer and get every idea down, then cluster and pick. Sketch quickly in Figma or FigJam.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: User story generation is writing needs as short statements from the user's point of view. It keeps the focus on the person, not the feature.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Stories break big requirements into small, buildable pieces the team can pick up one at a time.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in requirements and produces user story statements.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Write each need as who wants what and why, with clear acceptance criteria. Capture them in Notion or Trello.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

activities.Activity Description: Calculating statistics is crunching numbers to find patterns and check whether results are meaningful. It turns raw data into trustworthy findings.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Statistics keep a team from reading too much into noise or too little into a real trend.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in discovery and acceptance testing and feeds analytics audits and research analysis.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Choose the right measure for your question and run the numbers. Use statistics tools and sanity-check the results.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Measuring accessibility is checking whether a product works for people with a range of abilities. It tests how inclusive a design really is.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Building for everyone is both right and often required, and catching issues early beats retrofitting.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs across implement, launch, and acceptance testing and produces the accessibility analysis.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Check the product against accessibility standards and assistive tools, noting gaps. Record findings in Notion or FigJam.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Site map testing checks whether a product's structure helps people find things. It tests the map, not the visuals.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A structure that matches how users think prevents a lot of getting lost.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs across discovery, implement, and acceptance testing and feeds research reports and the sitemap.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Give users findability tasks and watch where they go. Run it in Notion or FigJam and refine the structure.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Copywriting is writing the words in a product and its marketing to guide and persuade people. Words do a lot of quiet work in a product.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Clear, well-crafted words guide users and build trust, while confusing ones lose them.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in the Implement work and produces the copywriting document and microcopy.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Write clearly for the reader, then trim anything extra. Draft in Figma or Notion, following the style guide.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Server-side coding builds the behind-the-scenes logic and data handling that powers a product. It is the engine users do not see.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Solid server-side work makes a product fast, reliable, and secure.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It produces code and the API library and supports development.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Build the logic and data handling for each feature, then test it. Work in your IDE.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

activities.Activity Description: Front-end coding builds the part of a product that users see and interact with. It turns designs into working screens.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: It is where design becomes something people can actually use.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It produces code, documentation, and the API library and supports development.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Turn the designs and specs into working, responsive screens. Build and test in your IDE.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

activities.Activity Description: Database creation is building the structure that stores and organizes a product's data. It is where the product's memory lives.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A well-built database keeps a product fast and reliable and prevents messy data problems.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in requirements and produces entity relationship diagrams and the database architecture.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Set up the tables and relationships from the data model, then test them. Build it in your IDE.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

activities.Activity Description: Creating illustrations is making custom visuals that bring a product or brand to life. They add personality words and photos cannot.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Good illustrations make a product feel distinct, warm, and memorable.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in the Implement work and produces logo and brand assets.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Sketch concepts that fit the brand, then refine the best in Figma.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Blockchain coding builds programs that run on a blockchain, like smart contracts. It is a specialized kind of development.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: It enables trusted, automatic transactions without a middleman, when a product needs that.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It produces code and smart contracts and supports development.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Write and carefully test the contract logic, since it is hard to change once live. Work in your IDE.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

activities.Activity Description: Collecting analytics is gathering data on how people actually use a product. It shows real behavior, not just opinions.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Usage data reveals what people really do, which often differs from what they say.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs across discovery, requirements, implement, and acceptance testing and feeds the UX audit and analytics audit.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Set up tracking for the actions that matter and gather the data. Review it in Notion.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Analyzing project risk is spotting what could go wrong and planning how to handle it. It is looking for trouble on purpose, early.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Spotting risks ahead of time lets a team prevent or soften problems instead of scrambling.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens across the project and feeds the project plan and risk analysis.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: List what could go wrong, rate each risk, and plan a response. Track it in Notion.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

activities.Activity Description: Primary research is gathering new data directly from users yourself, through interviews, tests, and the like. It is first-hand learning.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Direct research gives fresh, specific insight tailored to your exact questions.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs across discovery and acceptance testing and feeds journey maps, reports, and analysis.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Choose a method, gather data straight from users, and analyze it. Use tools like UXtweak and Figma.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Choosing research methods is picking the right way to study a question. Different questions call for different approaches.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: The right method gets a trustworthy answer efficiently, while the wrong one wastes effort.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in discovery and produces the research plan.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Match your question to a fitting method and check it is feasible. Decide it in Figma or UXtweak while planning.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Product backlog maintenance is keeping the backlog current, clear, and well-ordered. A backlog only helps if it stays healthy.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A tidy backlog means the team always knows what is worth doing next.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs through discovery and requirements and produces the refined backlog.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Regularly review, re-order, and clarify backlog items. Manage it in Notion.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

activities.Activity Description: Release vision definition is deciding what a specific release is really trying to achieve. It sets the point of the release.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A clear release vision keeps the work focused on an outcome, not just a list of features.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs across discovery, vision, and launch and feeds vision boards, the release plan, and the pitch deck.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Describe what the release should accomplish and why it matters. Shape it in Figma with the team.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

activities.Activity Description: Optimizing SEO is improving an existing product or site so it ranks better in search. It is tuning what is already there to be found more.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Better search visibility connects a product to the people already looking for it.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in the Implement work and produces the SEO strategy.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Review current performance, then improve content, structure, and keywords. Work in Notion and Figma.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Creating annotations is adding notes to a design that explain how it should work. It fills in what a picture alone cannot show.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Annotations make sure design intent survives the handoff to developers.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in the Implement work and produces UI development specifications and design annotations.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Mark up the design with clear notes on behavior and detail. Add them right in Figma.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

activities.Activity Description: Maintaining the client relationship is keeping communication clear and trust strong with the client throughout a project. It is the steady human connection behind the work.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: A healthy client relationship prevents misunderstandings and keeps a project on solid ground.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It runs across the project and produces the statement of work. It supports account and project management.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Check in regularly, set clear expectations, and follow through. Keep notes and agreements organized for reference.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

activities.Activity Description: Creating acceptance criteria is writing the plain conditions that define when work is done. It sets a shared finish line.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Agreed criteria end the debate about whether something is finished.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in requirements and produces acceptance criteria, task flows, and scope.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: For each item, list what must be true to accept it. Write them in Notion or Trello with the team.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

activities.Activity Description: Investigating competitors is studying similar products to learn what they do well and poorly. It reads the competitive field.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Knowing the competition helps a team find gaps to fill and mistakes to avoid.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens in discovery and produces the competitive analysis.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Review competing products against clear criteria and note the takeaways. Organize findings in a spreadsheet or Notion.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian's guide to product management: https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management

activities.Activity Description: Choosing an agile method is picking the way of working that fits the team, like Scrum or Kanban. It sets the team's rhythm.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: The right method gives everyone a shared, proven way to plan, build, and improve.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens at intake and produces the agile method decision.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Weigh the options against how the team works, then agree on one. Decide it together in Notion or FigJam.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Team Playbook, practical plays for healthy teamwork: https://www.atlassian.com/team-playbook

activities.Activity Description: Leading agile transformation is helping a team or organization shift to agile ways of working. It is guiding real change in how people work.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Done well, it makes a team faster, more collaborative, and more resilient.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens at intake and produces the RACI chart, process map, agile method, and team charter.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Assess how things work now, guide the team toward new habits, and support the change. Facilitate it in FigJam and track in Notion.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Team Playbook, practical plays for healthy teamwork: https://www.atlassian.com/team-playbook

activities.Activity Description: Defining research operations is setting up how a team's research work runs, from tools to templates to process. It is the behind-the-scenes support for research.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Good research ops make studies faster, more consistent, and easier to reuse.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens at intake and produces the team process map.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Standardize the tools, templates, and steps the research team uses. Document it in Notion or FigJam.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Team Playbook, practical plays for healthy teamwork: https://www.atlassian.com/team-playbook

activities.Activity Description: Defining UX design operations is setting up how a team's design work runs, from files to systems to process. It keeps design work organized and consistent.
activities.Why Is This Activity Important?: Solid design ops let designers focus on design instead of wrestling with process.
activities.How Does the Activity Relate to Mileston: It happens at intake and produces the team process map.
activities.How To Complete the Activity: Standardize the files, systems, and steps the design team uses. Document it in Notion or FigJam.
activities.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Team Playbook, practical plays for healthy teamwork: https://www.atlassian.com/team-playbook

duties.Duty Description: The UX Design duty is about shaping how a product actually works for the people using it, turning rough ideas into screens and flows that feel simple. Day to day that means sketching wireframes, building clickable prototypes, and pulling patterns together into a design system so the whole product feels like one coherent thing. Designers rarely work in a straight line; they try something, put it in front of people, and refine it as the team learns.
duties.What Does It Take for This Duty To Succe: It takes a mix of craft and people skills: interaction design, information architecture, and prototyping to build the work, plus the openness to share ownership and take feedback without ego. Comfort in tools like Figma and Figjam helps, but the real skill is staying curious about whether a design truly makes sense for a real person.
duties.Why Is This Duty Important to Project Su: Design is where a plan becomes something people can see and touch. This duty owns deliverables like wireframes and prototypes that the rest of the team builds on, and it stays active from early discovery through launch, so the product keeps improving instead of freezing at version one.
You might enjoy this duty if you like turning fuzzy problems into clear, usable designs, enjoy sketching and iterating, and get satisfaction from watching a rough idea become something people find easy to use.
duties.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

duties.Duty Description: The UX Research duty is the team's link to real users. Instead of guessing what people need, researchers plan and run studies, interviews, usability tests, and surveys, then turn what they hear into clear findings the whole team can act on. It is ongoing work; strong teams keep discovering all the way through a project rather than researching once and moving on.
duties.What Does It Take for This Duty To Succe: Succeeding here takes real research skills like interviewing, experiment design, and spotting patterns in messy data, along with the ability to tell a clear story with what you find. Just as important are the team habits: listening well, staying curious, and building enough trust that people share honest feedback.
duties.Why Is This Duty Important to Project Su: This duty keeps the team honest about what users actually need, so effort goes toward real problems instead of assumptions. Its research plans and reports feed decisions at every milestone, and by surfacing issues early it saves the team from building the wrong thing.
You might enjoy this duty if you are curious about people, like listening more than talking, and get a kick out of turning messy human behavior into clear insight the team can use.
duties.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/

duties.Duty Description: The Business Analysis duty turns fuzzy requests into a clear, shared picture of what to build. Analysts gather requirements, write user stories and acceptance criteria, and shape problem statements so everyone agrees on what needs to happen and how they will know it is done. In agile work they write just enough to get moving and keep refining as the team learns.
duties.What Does It Take for This Duty To Succe: It takes a knack for asking good questions and translating between people, plus skills like requirements management, writing user stories, and defining acceptance criteria. The strongest analysts pair that with patience, active listening, and the facilitation skills to get a room to agree.
duties.Why Is This Duty Important to Project Su: Clear requirements are one of the biggest reasons projects succeed or quietly fail. This duty produces the acceptance criteria and user stories the whole team builds against, so designers and developers stop working from different assumptions and expensive rework never happens.
You might enjoy this duty if you like untangling messy problems, enjoy detail, and are good at translating between what people say they want and what the team can actually build.
duties.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

duties.Duty Description: The Product Ownership duty decides what the team should build next and in what order. Owners maintain the backlog, prioritize the work, and keep a roadmap so the team always has a clear, ranked list to pull from. Priorities shift as the team learns, so this is constant, iterative work rather than a plan set once at the start.
duties.What Does It Take for This Duty To Succe: It takes sharp prioritization, backlog and epic management, and the judgment to say this now, that later, and explain why. Add strong stakeholder skills, since much of the job is balancing many voices and building buy-in for the plan.
duties.Why Is This Duty Important to Project Su: This duty keeps the team pointed at the most valuable work instead of doing a little of everything. By owning the backlog and sprint goals, it turns a big pile of ideas into a focused plan, which is what lets an agile team ship steadily.
You might enjoy this duty if you like making decisions, can weigh many priorities at once, and enjoy owning the details of getting the right thing delivered.

duties.Duty Description: The Product Management duty sets the direction for a product, the what and the why behind the work. Managers dig into users and the market, shape the vision and strategy, and rally the team around which problems are worth solving. They do not build it all themselves; they help everyone pull in the same direction.
duties.What Does It Take for This Duty To Succe: It takes strategic thinking, market and customer insight, and the storytelling to get people behind a vision. Because a manager works through others, the people skills, influence, negotiation, and clear communication, matter as much as the strategy itself.
duties.Why Is This Duty Important to Project Su: This duty makes sure the team is building something people actually want and the business can sustain. By owning the vision, roadmap, and go-to-market plan, it connects users, business, and technology so the whole project has a clear point.
You might enjoy this duty if you like strategy, enjoy connecting people, business, and technology, and are comfortable making calls with incomplete information.

duties.Duty Description: The Scrum Master duty helps a team run smoothly using agile methods like Scrum. Rather than managing people, scrum masters facilitate the rhythm of the work, sprint planning, retrospectives, and demos, and clear roadblocks so the team can focus. A lot of the job is protecting the process and helping the team keep improving.
duties.What Does It Take for This Duty To Succe: It takes facilitation skills, a solid grasp of Scrum, and the patience to guide without controlling. The best scrum masters are strong listeners and conflict-resolvers who help a team surface problems and fix them together.
duties.Why Is This Duty Important to Project Su: This duty keeps an agile team's engine running. By facilitating sprints and retrospectives, it helps the team deliver in steady cycles and get a little better each time, which is the whole point of working in an agile way.
You might enjoy this duty if you like helping a team work well together, enjoy facilitating over directing, and find satisfaction in removing the obstacles that slow people down.
duties.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

duties.Duty Description: The Project Management duty keeps the work organized and moving. Project managers track what needs to happen, watch the schedule and risks, and keep clients and teammates in the loop so nothing important slips. Much of the job is communication and clearing roadblocks before they slow the team down.
duties.What Does It Take for This Duty To Succe: It takes organization, clear communication, and the ability to stay calm when a lot is in motion. Skills like project management, meeting facilitation, and stakeholder management help, along with the people sense to keep everyone aligned.
duties.Why Is This Duty Important to Project Su: This duty is the glue that holds a project together. By tracking milestones, managing risk, and keeping the client relationship healthy, it lets the rest of the team focus on the work instead of the logistics.
You might enjoy this duty if you like structure, enjoy helping others do their best work, and stay level-headed when things get busy.
duties.Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Agile Coach, with guides on agile, Scrum, and Kanban: https://www.atlassian.com/agile

duties.Duty Description: The Development duty builds the product, turning designs and requirements into working software. Developers write and document code, build APIs and databases, and deploy what they make so it runs the way it should. It is problem-solving work, breaking a big challenge into small pieces and getting each one working, often in short cycles alongside the rest of the team.
duties.What Does It Take for This Duty To Succe: It takes solid technical skills, programming, database work, and API design, plus the logical thinking to debug problems methodically. The strongest developers also collaborate well, since building software is a team sport that depends on shared ownership and clear communication.
duties.Why Is This Duty Important to Project Su: This duty is where the product actually gets made. The code, APIs, and databases it produces are the working thing users rely on, so the care put in here shows up directly in whether the product holds together.
You might enjoy this duty if you like logic and building things, enjoy solving technical puzzles, and feel real satisfaction when something you made finally runs.
duties.Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

duties.Duty Description: The Solutions Architecture duty designs the technical foundation a product is built on. Architects map out how the system fits together, its databases, services, network, and hosting, so developers have a solid, scalable base to build against. It is big-picture technical work that shapes how well everything else holds up.
duties.What Does It Take for This Duty To Succe: It takes deep systems thinking and strong skills in database and network architecture, plus the ability to weigh trade-offs and explain them clearly. Good architects balance what is ideal with what the team can realistically build and maintain.
duties.Why Is This Duty Important to Project Su: This duty sets the technical direction that everything else depends on. A sound architecture lets the product scale and stay stable, while a shaky one causes problems that surface long after launch, so getting it right early matters.
You might enjoy this duty if you like seeing the whole system at once, enjoy solving structural puzzles, and care about building something that will hold up as it grows.
duties.Where Can I Learn More?: MDN Web Docs, a trusted resource for building software: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn

duties.Duty Description: The Information Security Analysis duty protects a product and its users from threats. Analysts model how something could be attacked, test for weaknesses, configure defenses, and audit the system to keep data safe. It is careful, detail-driven work that looks for problems before someone with bad intent does.
duties.What Does It Take for This Duty To Succe: It takes a security mindset, network knowledge, and the patience to probe a system for weak spots. Strong analysts pair technical skill with clear communication, since much of the job is explaining risks in a way the team can act on.
duties.Why Is This Duty Important to Project Su: This duty keeps trust intact. A single security gap can undo a lot of good work and harm the people a product serves, so by finding and closing weaknesses early, this duty protects both users and the team's reputation.
You might enjoy this duty if you like thinking like a puzzle-solver, enjoy finding weak spots others miss, and care about keeping people and their data safe.
duties.Where Can I Learn More?: OWASP, the open community for software security: https://owasp.org/

duties.Duty Description: The UX Writing duty crafts the words inside a product, the buttons, labels, messages, and instructions that guide people along. Writers shape a clear voice, build style guides, and cut anything confusing so the product feels simple to use. It sounds small, but the right words can make or break whether people understand what to do.
duties.What Does It Take for This Duty To Succe: It takes a love of clear language, strong writing and editing skills, and an eye for how words fit into a design. Add empathy and collaboration, since good UX writing comes from understanding users and working closely with designers and researchers.
duties.Why Is This Duty Important to Project Su: This duty is what makes a product feel clear instead of confusing. Its words appear at every step users take, so strong writing quietly guides people through the experience and reduces the friction that makes them give up.
You might enjoy this duty if you love words, care about making things easy to understand, and enjoy finding the simplest way to say something.
duties.Where Can I Learn More?: Nielsen Norman Group, a trusted source for UX research and design: https://www.nngroup.com/
